title: Effects of hypochlorous acid and sodium hypochlorite irrigation protocols, used alone or combined with ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid, on root canal dentin: An in vitro study
content:
by Nuria Simo, Ana Paredes, Álvaro Villanueva, James Ghilotti, Carmen Llena

Objective

This in vitro study evaluated the effect of irrigation protocols based on 5.25% sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) or 200 ppm hypochlorous acid (HOCl), used alone or combined with 17% ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA), on smear layer removal, open dentinal tubules and erosion of root canal dentin.

Methods

Forty-five palatal or distal roots of human molars were instrumented to size 50/.06 and randomly allocated to NaOCl + EDTA, NaOCl, HOCl + EDTA or HOCl (n = 10 each) or to a saline negative control (n = 5). Canals received 2 mL of irrigant after each instrument and a final sequence with 3 mL of each solution for 20 s. Root thirds were examined by scanning electron microscopy. A trained, calibrated and blinded examiner (weighted κ = 0.88) scored smear layer and erosion on ordinal scales; open tubules were quantified by digital image segmentation.

Results

Smear layer scores differed among groups only in the middle third (p = 0.013), where NaOCl + EDTA left less smear layer than NaOCl alone (p = 0.008); HOCl + EDTA did not differ significantly from HOCl alone or from NaOCl + EDTA in any third. In both combined protocols smear layer was greatest apically (p < 0.001). Images completely covered by smear layer could not be segmented, so open tubules were quantified in only 20–23 of 45 specimens per third, without significant differences between the combined protocols. Erosion was assessable in only 28 of 135 images and was reported descriptively.

Conclusions

With syringe irrigation, neither chlorine-based irrigant removed the smear layer without a chelator. EDTA significantly reduced smear layer with 5.25% NaOCl, but no significant contribution was detected with 200 ppm HOCl in this sample. These findings do not support replacing NaOCl with HOCl and agree with existing evidence supporting NaOCl followed by EDTA as the reference protocol.
